e202.text: A metal spoon sinks. But a giant metal ship floats! What is inside the ship that helps it to float? One, wood. Two, air. Three, more metal.

e301.text: You against the Buddies! Lock in first. One finger for every point. A little otter is hiding in this video. Can you spot it?

h501.text: Are you ready? Three! Two! One! Go!

e501.text: Two blocks, the same size. One is wood. One is metal. Look closer.

e502.text: The wooden block bobs up. It floats.

e503.text: The metal block goes straight down. It sinks.

e504.text: Now two spoons. The wooden spoon floats. The metal spoon sinks.

e505.text: Most types of wood float on water. Most metals sink in water.

e506.text: Same size. Same shape. Different material!

e601.text: Is this the rule? Heavy things sink, and light things float!

e602.text: Something is not right. If you can spot it, cross your arms. Hold on!

e603.text: Arms crossed? One finger up! The giant ship is very heavy, and it floats. The little spoon is light, and it sinks.

e606.text: The material of an object affects the ability of the object to float or sink.

e701.text: But a ship is metal. And metal sinks!

e702.text: Round one: the question from last time! What is inside the ship? Wood, air, or more metal? Show me your fingers!

e704.text: One. Wood floats, so there must be wood inside.

e705.text: Two! Air! My swimming float is full of air!

e801.text: Look closer. Here is the giant metal ship. Part of it sits under the water.

e802.text: A window opens in its side. Look inside. Big rooms. Tall spaces. All full of air.

e803.text: Now the metal block. Solid metal. No air inside. It sank.

e901.text: Be the air! Shrink down. Quietly.

e902.text: You are air, drifting over the sea.

e903.text: You float in through a door, into a giant metal ship.

e904.text: A huge room. Metal walls all around you.

e905.text: The door shuts. You are trapped air!

e906.text: Outside the wall: deep water. Inside: you.

e907.text: The ship floats on. You are helping!

e1001.text: Why does a metal ship float?

e1003.text: This is because there is a lot of trapped air inside the ship. The trapped air helps the ship to float on water.

e1101.text: Now, a metal bowl. Look closer.

e1102.text: It floats, like a little ship. Air is inside it.

e1103.text: Now water pours in. The water takes the place of the air.

e1104.text: The bowl sits lower. And lower. It sinks!

e1201.text: Show me your score hand! More than one? You beat the Buddies. Two fingers? High five!

e1202.text: Did you spot the otter? It was swimming by the rocks! Tell someone at home.

h860.text: Let's read today's key words together! Ready?

e1301.text: Rain! Oh no, my school shoes!

e1302.text: A plastic raincoat. A fabric school shoe. Rain falls on both. Which one does the water soak into?
